claim: CD4+ T cells expressing granzyme B (CD4+GzB+ T cells) represent around 30% of CD4+ T cells in the spleen of C57BL/6 mice during acute phase of Trypanosoma cruzi infection.
source: Here, we reveal the presence of a TCRαβ+CD8α-NK1.1-CD4+GzB+ T cell population, which represents around 30% of the CD4+ T cells in the spleen of C57BL/6 (B6) mice, in the acute phase of infection with T. cruzi (Figure 1A and B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1A and B, which demonstrates the frequency of CD4+GzB+ T cells in infected mice.

claim: Equivalent percentages of CD4+PRF+ T cells are found in the spleen of infected mice.
source: Equivalent percentages of CD4+PRF+ T cells were found (Figure 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1C demonstrating perforin expression in CD4+ T cells.

claim: The majority of CD4+GzB+ T cells express perforin (PRF) and the cytolytic marker 2B4 (CD244).
source: the majority of CD4+GzB+ T cells express PRF and the cytolytic marker 2B4 (CD244) (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1D and E showing co-expression of PRF and 2B4 on CD4+GzB+ T cells.

claim: Most CD4+GzB+ T cells (>80%) do not express IFN-γ at day 14 post-infection.
source: Of note, most CD4+GzB+ T cells (>80%) do not express IFN-γ at day 14 post-infection (pi), the peak time-point of the T cell response
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing the percentage of CD4+GzB+ T cells that are IFN-γ negative.

claim: The absolute number of CD4+GzB+ T cells is superior to that of CD4+IFN-γ+ cells at every time point of infection.
source: although CD4GzB+ and CD4IFN-γ+ cells follow similar kinetics in the spleen, the absolute number of CD4+GzB+ T cells was superior to that of CD4+IFN-γ+ cells, at every time point of the infection (Figure 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by kinetic data shown in Figure 1G comparing absolute numbers of CD4+GzB+ and CD4+IFN-γ+ T cells over time.

claim: Intracellular parasitism by T. cruzi Y strain in the spleen is at its highest point between day 12 and 15 post-infection.
source: It is known that intracellular parasitism by T. cruzi Y strain in the spleen is at its highest point between day 12 and 15 pi, concomitant with the histologically observed massive destruction of parasitized splenic macrophages (Cordeiro et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work by Cordeiro et al., 1997.

claim: There is a coincidence between parasite titers in the spleen and the frequency and absolute numbers of CD4+GzB+ T cells.
source: Therefore, there is a coincidence between parasite titers in the spleen and the frequency and absolute numbers of CD4+GzB+ T cells.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the temporal correlation between peak parasitism (day 12-15) and peak CD4+GzB+ T cell numbers.

claim: An increase in the percentage of degranulating CD4+ T cells is observed at day 14 post-infection, comparable to CD8+ T cells, as inferred by staining with anti-CD107a (LAMP-1) mAb.
source: We also observed an increase in the percentage of degranulating CD4+ T cells at day 14 pi, comparable to the CD8+ T cells, as inferred by staining with anti-CD107a (LAMP-1) mAb, (Figure 1H)
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1H showing LAMP-1 expression on CD4+ and CD8+ T cells.

claim: CD8+ cytotoxic T cells are present at higher percentage and absolute number than CD4+GzB+ T cells in infected spleens.
source: although CD8CTLs are present at higher percentage (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B-E and G ) and absolute number (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1 supplement 1 comparing CD4+ and CD8+ GzB+ T cell frequencies and numbers.

claim: Effector CD4+ T cells from infected mice exert cytotoxic activity against anti-CD3 mAb-coated B cell blasts.
source: To ascertain the presence of CD4+ T lymphocytes with cytolytic function, we performed a redirected cytotoxicity assay, with anti-CD3 mAb–coated B cell blasts as target cells that were co-incubated with either highly purified effector (CD44hi) CD4 T cells sorted from the spleen of infected mice or naive (CD44lo) CD4 T cells from non-infected controls. The CTL activity was observed only when effector CD4+ T cells were employed (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 2A demonstrating killing of target cells by effector CD4+ T cells.

claim: The killing of target cells by CD4+ T cells is abolished in the presence of granzyme B and perforin inhibitors.
source: In order to determine if the CD4CTL killing capability is dependent on GzB- and PRF-mediated killing, we performed the cytotoxic assays in the presence of the GzB and PRF inhibitors, Z-AAD-CMK and Concamycin A, respectively. As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, the killing of target cells was abolished in this condition
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data in Figure 2 supplement 1A showing loss of killing activity with inhibitors.

claim: The cytolysis mediated by CD4CTLs in T. cruzi-infected mice depends on granzyme B and perforin.
source: the killing of target cells was abolished in this condition, demonstrating that the cytolysis mediated by CD4CTLs in T. cruzi-infected mice depends on GzB and PRF, as previously shown for tumor-specific CD4CTLs (Quezada et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with inhibitors and by citation to previous work on tumor-specific CD4CTLs (Quezada et al., 2010).

claim: CD4CTLs with cognate cytotoxic activity against T. cruzi amastigote antigens are present in the spleen of infected mice.
source: Antigen-specific cytotoxicity, using highly purified CD4+ T cells, was also assayed in vitro against an I-Ab+ macrophage cell line (IC-21), loaded or not with T. cruzi amastigote total protein extract. Results shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B demonstrate that CD4CTLs with cognate cytotoxic activity are present in the spleen of infected mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by antigen-specific cytotoxicity assay data in Figure 2B showing killing of antigen-loaded target cells.

claim: Addition of anti-FasL mAb significantly inhibits the specific lysis of target cells by CD4CTLs.
source: As shown in Figure 2B, addition of anti-FasL mAb significantly inhibited the specific lysis of the target cells, demonstrating the involvement of the FasL/Fas pathway in the killing process.
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data in Figure 2B showing reduced killing with anti-FasL antibody.

claim: FasL is expressed on CD8+ and CD4+ T cells at the immunological synapse following Ag-triggered degranulation and participates in CD4CTL-mediated lysis of target cells.
source: FasL is expressed on CD8+ and CD4+ T cells at the immunological synapse following Ag-triggered degranulation and participates in CD4CTL-mediated lysis of target cells (Bossi and Griffiths, 1999; Brown et al., 2009; Kotov et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Bossi and Griffiths, 1999; Brown et al., 2009; Kotov et al., 2018).

claim: In vivo killing of target splenocytes loaded with class II-restricted T. cruzi-derived peptides (SA85-1.1c and d) is observed in infected mice.
source: We tested the in vivo killing of target splenocytes loaded with class II-restricted peptides (SA85-1.1c and d), derived from a protein of the T. cruzi transialidase superfamily (Millar and Kahn, 2000; Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo cytotoxicity assay data in Figure 2C showing specific killing of peptide-loaded targets.

claim: The same level of specific killing is attained against targets loaded with class I- or class II-restricted OVA peptides in mice infected with OVA-expressing Y strain trypomastigotes.
source: To circumvent this, we infected mice with ovalbumin (OVA)-expressing Y strain trypomastigotes (Y-OVA) (Gomes-Neto et al., 2018) and compared the in vivo cytotoxic response against known OVA-derived CD4 and CD8 epitopes: OVA323-339 and OVA257-264, respectively. As shown in Figure 2D, the same level of specific killing was attained against targets loaded with class I- or class II-restricted OVA peptides.
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo cytotoxicity assay data in Figure 2D comparing killing of class I and class II peptide-loaded targets.

claim: The vast majority of CD4+GzB+ T cells express T-bet, but not FoxP3.
source: Figure 2E and F show that the vast majority of CD4+GzB+ T cells express T-bet, but not FoxP3, the master gene of Treg cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2E and F showing T-bet and FoxP3 expression patterns.

claim: 60% of CD4+GzB+ T cells express Eomesodermin (Eomes).
source: In accordance with the cytolytic potential of CD4+GzB+ T cells in our model, 60% of the CD4+GzB+ T cells express Eomes, while only a small percentage of GzB- CD4+ T cells are Eomes+ (Figure 2G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2G showing Eomes expression in CD4+GzB+ T cells.

claim: At day 14 post-infection, the vast majority of both GzB+ and GzB- CD4+ T lymphocytes are CD44hiCD62Llo effector/memory cells.
source: Of note, at day 14 pi, the vast majority of both GzB+ and GzB- CD4+ T lymphocytes are CD44hiCD62Llo effector/memory cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2 supplement 2 showing CD44 and CD62L expression patterns.

claim: CD4+GzB+ T cells sorted from infected GzmbCreERT2/ROSA26EYFP reporter mice express Runx3d mRNA.
source: As shown in Figure 2H, besides Runx3d mRNA, we found that CD4+GzB+ T cells, sorted from the spleen of tamoxifen-treated infected GzmbCreERT2/ROSA26EYFP reporter mice (Bannard et al., 2009; Figure 2—figure supplement 3A), express ThPOK (Zbtb7b gene)-coding RNA comparable to naive CD4+ T cells, at day 14 pi
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 2H showing Runx3d expression in sorted CD4+GzB+ T cells.

claim: CD4+GzB+ T cells express ThPOK (Zbtb7b gene)-coding RNA comparable to naive CD4+ T cells at day 14 post-infection.
source: we found that CD4+GzB+ T cells, sorted from the spleen of tamoxifen-treated infected GzmbCreERT2/ROSA26EYFP reporter mice (Bannard et al., 2009; Figure 2—figure supplement 3A), express ThPOK (Zbtb7b gene)-coding RNA comparable to naive CD4+ T cells, at day 14 pi, when their number and frequency are at the highest levels in this organ (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 2H showing ThPOK expression levels in CD4+GzB+ T cells.

claim: The absence of CD8α-coding transcripts confirms the purity of sorted CD4+GzB+ T cells.
source: The absence of CD8α-coding transcripts confirms the purity of sorted CD4+GzB+ T cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 2 supplement 3B showing no CD8α expression in sorted cells.

claim: T-bet and Eomesodermin (Eomes) bind to the promoters of Gzmb and Prf1.
source: T-bet and Eomesodermin (Eomes) are known to bind to the promoters of Gzmb and Prf1 (Glimcher et al., 2004; Intlekofer et al., 2005; Pearce et al., 2003)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Glimcher et al., 2004; Intlekofer et al., 2005; Pearce et al., 2003).

claim: T-bet and Eomes are expressed in CD4CTLs.
source: T-bet and Eomesodermin (Eomes) are known to bind to the promoters of Gzmb and Prf1 (Glimcher et al., 2004; Intlekofer et al., 2005; Pearce et al., 2003) and were shown to be expressed in CD4CTLs (Curran et al., 2013; Eshima et al., 2012; Qui et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Curran et al., 2013; Eshima et al., 2012; Qui et al., 2011).

claim: CD4CTLs that migrate to the gut gradually stop expressing ThPOK while upregulating the expression of RUNX3.
source: CD4CTLs that migrate to the gut, gradually stop expressing ThPOK, while upregulating the expression of RUNX3 (Mucida et al., 2013; Reis et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Mucida et al., 2013; Reis et al., 2013).

claim: RUNX3 drives the CTL gene program in CD8+ T cells.
source: RUNX3 (Mucida et al., 2013; Reis et al., 2013), which is known to drive the CTL gene program in CD8+ T cells (Cruz-Guilloty et al., 2009; Egawa et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Cruz-Guilloty et al., 2009; Egawa et al., 2007).

claim: The long-form transcript encoding RUNX3 (Runx3d) is expressed in Th1 cells, but not in Th2 or naïve cells.
source: The long-form transcript encoding RUNX3 (Runx3d) is also expressed in Th1 cells, but not in Th2 or naïve cells (Djuretic et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Djuretic et al., 2007).

claim: A very low frequency of IL-10-producing TCRαβ+CD4+ T cells is detected in the spleens of mice infected with T. cruzi.
source: We detected a very low frequency of IL-10-producing TCRαβ+CD4+ T cells in the spleens of mice infected with T. cruzi, in agreement with previous data (Jankovic et al., 2007)
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data and citation to previous work (Jankovic et al., 2007).

claim: IL-10+ cells are more frequent among CD4+GzB+ T cells than among total CD4+ T cells.
source: although IL-10+ cells were found to be more frequent among CD4+GzB+ T cells (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3A showing IL-10 expression in CD4+GzB+ T cells.

claim: The co-expression of Lag-3 and CD49b defines both human and mouse Tr1 cells.
source: The co-expression of Lag-3 and CD49b defines both human and mouse Tr1 cells (Gagliani et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Gagliani et al., 2013).

claim: Most splenic CD4+GzB+ T cells express Lag-3, but only a minor percentage co-express CD49b.
source: Although most splenic CD4+GzB+ T cells express Lag-3, only a minor percentage of these cells co-express CD49b (Figure 3B and C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3B and C showing Lag-3 and CD49b expression patterns.

claim: A substantial fraction of splenic CD4+GzB+ T cells express the immunoregulatory molecule Tim-3 and downregulate CD27.
source: On the other hand, a substantial fraction of splenic CD4+GzB+ T cells express the immunoregulatory molecule Tim-3 and downregulate CD27 (Figure 3D and E)
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3D and E showing Tim-3 and CD27 expression patterns.

claim: CD4+GzB+ T cells that downregulate CD27 and express Tim-3 might be terminally differentiated cells.
source: a substantial fraction of splenic CD4+GzB+ T cells express the immunoregulatory molecule Tim-3 and downregulate CD27 (Figure 3D and E), indicating that these might be terminally differentiated cells, as suggested in other models (Anderson et al., 2016; Takeuchi and Saito, 2017).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from marker expression patterns and citations to previous studies (Anderson et al., 2016; Takeuchi and Saito, 2017).

claim: The frequency of cells expressing NKG2A/C/E and NKG2D is increased among splenic CD4+GzB+ T cells compared to GzB- CD4+ T cells of infected mice or naive CD4+ T cells of non-infected controls.
source: As shown in Figure 3F and G , the fraction of cells expressing NKG2A/C/E and NKG2D was increased among splenic CD4+GzB+ T cells, when compared to either GzB- CD4+ T cells of infected mice or to naive CD4+ T cells of non-infected controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3F and G showing NKG2A/C/E and NKG2D expression.

claim: The frequency of CRTAM-expressing cells is increased among splenic CD4+GzB+ T cells compared with GzB- CD4+ T cells.
source: Figure 3H shows that the frequency of CRTAM-expressing cells was also increased among splenic CD4+GzB+ T cells of T. cruzi-infected mice, when compared with GzB- CD4+ T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3H showing CRTAM expression.

claim: CRTAM is critical for the differentiation of CD4CTLs.
source: The class I-restricted T cell associated molecule (CRTAM) was described as being critical for the differentiation of CD4CTLs (Takeuchi et al., 2016; Takeuchi and Saito, 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Takeuchi et al., 2016; Takeuchi and Saito, 2017).

claim: Most NKG2D+ CD4+GzB+ T cells also express the CRTAM cytotoxic marker.
source: As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3, while most NKG2D+ cells also express the CRTAM cytotoxic marker, only a minority of CD4+GzB+ T cells co-express CRTAM and NKG2A/C/E molecules.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 3 supplement 3 showing co-expression patterns.

claim: Only a minority of CD4+GzB+ T cells co-express CRTAM and NKG2A/C/E molecules.
source: while most NKG2D+ cells also express the CRTAM cytotoxic marker, only a minority of CD4+GzB+ T cells co-express CRTAM and NKG2A/C/E molecules.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing co-expression patterns.

claim: Il12p40-/- mice infected with T. cruzi display lower percentages of T-bet+CD4+ and IFN-γ+CD4+ T cells and very low levels of CD4+GzB+ T cells.
source: Here, we observed that Il12p40-/- mice infected with T. cruzi displayed lower percentages of T-bet+CD4+ and IFN-γ+CD4+ T cells and exhibited very low levels of CD4+GzB+ T cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4A comparing WT and Il12p40-/- mice.

claim: In infected Ifng-/- mice, despite the lower frequency of T-bet+CD4+ T cells, CD4+GzB+ T cells attain the same frequencies as observed in the spleens of WT animals.
source: Interestingly, in infected Ifng-/- mice, despite the lower frequency of T-bet+CD4+ T cells, CD4+GzB+ T cells attained the same frequencies as observed in the spleens of WT animals (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4B comparing WT and Ifng-/- mice.

claim: Both GzB+ and total CD4+ T-cell numbers are significantly lower in infected Ifng-/- mice compared to WT controls.
source: However, absolute numbers of both total CD4+ and CD4+GzB+ T cells were lower in Ifng-/- mice when compared to WT controls.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data comparing absolute cell numbers in WT and Ifng-/- mice.

claim: Infected Myd88-/- mice display equivalent absolute numbers and percentages of total splenic CD4+ T cells compared to WT mice.
source: Although infected Myd88-/- mice displayed equivalent absolute numbers and percentages of total splenic CD4+ T cells when compared to WT mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4 supplement 1A comparing WT and Myd88-/- mice.

claim: The frequencies and absolute numbers of CD4+GzB+ T cells are significantly lower in Myd88-/- mice compared to WT mice.
source: the frequencies and absolute numbers of CD4+GzB+ T cells were significantly lower in this mouse strain (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4C-E comparing WT and Myd88-/- mice.

claim: Absolute numbers of CRTAM+, NKG2D+ and NKG2A/C/E+ CD4+GzB+ T cells are severely diminished in Myd88-/- mice.
source: Furthermore, absolute numbers of CRTAM+, NKG2D+ and NKG2A/C/E+ CD4+GzB+ T cells were severely diminished in Myd88-/- mice (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4C-E showing reduced numbers of cytotoxic marker-expressing cells.

claim: Absolute numbers of CRTAM+, NKG2D+ and NKG2A/C/E+ CD8+GzB+ T cells are not affected in Myd88-/- mice.
source: On the other hand, absolute numbers of CRTAM+, NKG2D+ and NKG2A/C/E+ CD8+GzB+ T cells were not affected in Myd88-/- mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4 supplement 1C-D comparing CD8+ T cells in WT and Myd88-/- mice.

claim: Both the percentages and absolute numbers of PRF+CD4+ T cells are severely decreased in Myd88-/- compared to WT mice.
source: Concerning the expression of perforin, both the percentages and absolute numbers of PRF+CD4+ T cells were also severely decreased in Myd88-/- compared to WT mice (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4F comparing perforin expression in WT and Myd88-/- mice.

claim: The frequency and absolute numbers of PRF+CD4+ T cells among GzB-expressing cells are severely decreased in Myd88-/- compared to WT mice.
source: The same was observed when analyzing the frequency and absolute numbers of PRF+CD4+ T cells among GzB-expressing cells (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 4G showing perforin expression among GzB+ cells.

claim: Lower levels of cytotoxicity are observed when sorted Myd88-/- CD4+CD44hi T cells are employed compared to assays using equal numbers of sorted WT CD4+CD44hi T cells.
source: In order to establish to what extent the absence of MyD88 expression would impact on cytotoxicity mediated by CD4+ T splenocytes, we sorted activated CD4+CD44hi T cells from both WT and Myd88-/- infected mice to a high purity level and performed redirected cytotoxicity assay. Lower levels of cytotoxicity were observed when sorted Myd88-/- CD4+CD44hi T cells were employed, as compared to assays using equal numbers of sorted WT CD4+CD44hi T cells (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data in Figure 4H comparing WT and Myd88-/- CD4+ T cells.

claim: MyD88 signaling is important for the establishment of a robust cytotoxic response mediated by CD4CTLs.
source: Together, these results demonstrate the important role of MyD88 signaling for the establishment of a robust cytotoxic response mediated by CD4CTLs.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental results showing reduced CD4CTL numbers and function in Myd88-/- mice.

claim: IL-18R/MyD88 signaling intrinsic to CD4+ T cells is critical for Th1 cell proliferation and resistance to apoptosis in response to infection with T. cruzi.
source: However, we have recently shown that IL-18R/MyD88 signaling intrinsic to CD4+ T cells is critical for Th1 cell proliferation and resistance to apoptosis in response to infection with T. cruzi (Oliveira et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Oliveira et al., 2017).

claim: 51 genes of the CD4CTL signature are upregulated in WT CD4+ T cells, while 78 are downregulated in Myd88-/- CD4+ T cells in mixed bone marrow chimeras.
source: Importantly, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), comparing the transcriptome of sorted WT and Myd88-/- CD4+ T cells, revealed that 51 genes of the CD4CTL signature were upregulated in WT CD4+ T cells, while 78 were downregulated in Myd88-/- CD4+ T cells (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5A-C comparing gene expression in WT and Myd88-/- CD4+ T cells.

claim: Blimp-1 (Prdm1 gene) transcription factor is upregulated in WT CD4+GzB+ T cells.
source: We confirmed, by flow cytometry, the upregulation of Blimp-1 (Prdm1 gene) TF and of the ecto-nucleotidase CD39 (Entpd1) in WT CD4+GzB+ T cells (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5D showing Blimp-1 expression.

claim: The ecto-nucleotidase CD39 (Entpd1) is upregulated in WT CD4+GzB+ T cells.
source: We confirmed, by flow cytometry, the upregulation of Blimp-1 (Prdm1 gene) TF and of the ecto-nucleotidase CD39 (Entpd1) in WT CD4+GzB+ T cells (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5E showing CD39 expression.

claim: Blimp-1 is required for the cytotoxic function of CD4CTLs.
source: Of note, Blimp-1 is required for the cytotoxic function of CD4CTLs (Hua et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Hua et al., 2013).

claim: CD39 expression level is higher in CD4+GzB+ T cells than in Tregs.
source: and CD39 expression level was found to be higher in CD4+GzB+ T cells than in Tregs (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5E comparing CD39 expression levels.

claim: The lack of IL-18R signaling in T cells, but not of IL-1R, phenocopies the absence of T cell-intrinsic MyD88 signaling in mixed bone marrow chimeras.
source: Figure 5F shows that the lack of IL-18R signaling in T cells, but not of IL-1R, phenocopied the absence of T cell-intrinsic MyD88 signaling, revealing that IL-18R is a critical pathway upstream MyD88 necessary for the establishment of the CD4+GzB+ T cell population.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5F comparing different chimera groups.

claim: IL-18R is a critical pathway upstream MyD88 necessary for the establishment of the CD4+GzB+ T cell population.
source: revealing that IL-18R is a critical pathway upstream MyD88 necessary for the establishment of the CD4+GzB+ T cell population.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from mixed bone marrow chimera experiments showing that IL-18R deficiency phenocopies MyD88 deficiency.

claim: Both the frequency and absolute number of PRF+CD4+ T cells are significantly diminished in the spleens of infected Il18ra-/- compared to WT mice.
source: Figure 6A shows that both the frequency and absolute number of PRF+CD4+ T cells were significantly diminished in the spleens of infected Il18ra-/- compared to WT mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6A comparing WT and Il18ra-/- mice.

claim: The frequency and absolute number of PRF-expressing cells among GzB+CD4+ T lymphocytes are decreased in infected Il18ra-/- compared to WT mice.
source: The same was true for PRF-expressing cells among GzB+CD4+ T lymphocytes (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6B showing perforin expression among GzB+ cells.

claim: The frequency of GzB+CD4+ T cells and their absolute number are decreased in infected Il18ra-/- compared to WT mice.
source: As observed in infected Myd88-/- mice, the frequency of GzB+CD4+ T cells and their absolute number were also decreased in infected Il18ra-/- compared to WT mice (Figure 6C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6C-E comparing WT and Il18ra-/- mice.

claim: Absolute numbers of CRTAM+, NKG2D+ and NKG2A/C/E+ GzB+CD4+ T cells are significantly diminished in Il18ra-/- mice.
source: Absolute numbers of CRTAM+, NKG2D+ and NKG2A/C/E+ GzB+CD4+ T cells were significantly diminished in Il18ra-/- mice as well, again phenocopying results obtained in Myd88-/- mice (Figure 6C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6C-E showing reduced numbers of cytotoxic marker-expressing cells.

claim: Lower levels of target killing are observed when employing purified Il18ra-/- CD4+CD44hi T cells as effectors compared to WT cells.
source: The cytotoxic potential of CD4+ T splenocytes from Il18ra-/- infected animals was also evaluated by performing redirected cytotoxicity assays with equal numbers of CD4+CD44hi T cells purified from infected Il18ra-/- or WT mice. Again, as shown for Myd88-/- CD4+ T cells, lower levels of target killing were observed when employing purified Il18ra-/- CD4+CD44hi T cells as effectors (Figure 6F).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data in Figure 6F comparing WT and Il18ra-/- CD4+ T cells.

claim: T-cell intrinsic IL-18R/MyD88 signaling supports the generation and/or survival of CD4+ T cells with cytotoxic potential in response to parasite infection.
source: Collectively, the present data demonstrate that T-cell intrinsic IL-18R/MyD88 signaling support the generation and/or survival of CD4+ T cells with cytotoxic potential in response to parasite infection
evidence: The claim is based on inference from multiple experimental results in Il18ra-/- and Myd88-/- mice.

claim: There is a parallel between the requirements for the development of robust Th1 and CD4CTL responses.
source: revealing a parallel between the requirements for the development of robust Th1 and CD4CTL responses.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the similar dependence of both cell types on IL-18R/MyD88 signaling.

claim: The transfer of highly purified CD4+GzB+(EYFP+) T cells to Il18ra-/- mice significantly extends their survival rate without decreasing the parasite load in the hearts.
source: The transfer of highly purified CD4+GzB+(EYFP+) T cells to Il18ra-/- mice significantly extended their survival rate without, however, decreasing the parasite load in the hearts (Figure 6G).
evidence: The claim is supported by survival curve and parasite load data in Figure 6G from adoptive transfer experiments.

claim: Adoptive transfer of CD4+ T cells sorted from Ifng-/- mice extends the survival of recipient Il18ra-/- mice.
source: Since infected Ifng-/- mice have the same frequency of CD4+GzB+ T cells as WT mice in their spleens (Figure 4B), we tested whether adoptive transfer of CD4+ T cells sorted from Ifng-/- mice would also be able to extend the survival of recipient Il18ra-/- mice. As shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2, this was indeed the case.
evidence: The claim is supported by survival curve data in Figure 6 supplement 2 from adoptive transfer experiments.

claim: The secretion of IFN-γ by adoptively transferred CD4+ T cells is not absolutely required for extending the survival time of infected Il18ra-/- recipients.
source: Although IFN-γ expression by CD4+ T cells is necessary for decreasing parasitemia (Oliveira et al., 2017), the present result indicated that the secretion of IFN-γ by adoptively transferred CD4+ T cells is not absolutely required for extending the survival time of infected Il18ra-/- recipients.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the adoptive transfer experiment with Ifng-/- CD4+ T cells and citation to previous work (Oliveira et al., 2017).

claim: The beneficial function of the CD4+GzB+ T cell subset against mortality caused by an intracellular parasite is independent of decreasing heart parasitism.
source: Together, these data demonstrate the beneficial function of the CD4+GzB+ T cell subset against mortality caused by an intracellular parasite, which is independent of decreasing heart parasitism.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from adoptive transfer experiments showing extended survival without reduced parasite load.

claim: CD4+GzB+ T cells infiltrating the cardiac tissue constitute the vast majority of CD4+CD44hi T cells.
source: As shown in Figure 7A and B and Figure 7—figure supplement 2, CD4+GzB+ T cells infiltrating the cardiac tissue constitute the vast majority of CD4+CD44hi T cells, indicating the enrichment of this subset among activated CD4+ T cells in the heart compared to the spleen.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7A, B and supplement 2 comparing heart and spleen.

claim: CD4+GzB+ T cells in the myocardium express the LAMP-1 degranulation marker at levels comparable to those of CD8+ T cells at the peak time-point of parasite load in the heart.
source: At the peak time-point of parasite load in the heart, CD4+GzB+ T cells in the myocardium express the LAMP-1 degranulation marker at levels comparable to those of CD8+ T cells (Figure 7C and D and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7C, D and supplement 1C showing LAMP-1 expression.

claim: The great majority of heart-infiltrating CD4+GzB+ T cells express PRF, CRTAM and NKG2D cytotoxic markers.
source: Importantly, the great majority of heart-infiltrating CD4+GzB+ T cells expresses PRF, as well as the CRTAM and NKG2D cytotoxic markers (Figure 7E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7E and F showing marker expression in heart-infiltrating cells.

claim: Only few CD4+GzB+ T cells express NKG2A/C/E in the myocardium.
source: On the other hand, only few CD4+GzB+ T cells express NKG2A/C/E in the myocardium (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7 supplement 1D showing NKG2A/C/E expression.

claim: There is a selective migration to, or retention in, the infected heart of double positive CRTAM+NKG2D+ CD4+GzB+ T cells.
source: These data indicate a selective migration to, or retention in, the infected heart of double positive CRTAM+NKG2D+ CD4+GzB+ T cells
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the differential expression patterns of cytotoxic markers in heart versus spleen.

claim: High percentages of NKG2A/C/E+CD8+GzB+ T cells are found both in the heart and in the spleen of infected mice.
source: On the other hand, high percentages of NKG2A/C/E+CD8+GzB+ T cells were found both in the heart (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D, right) and in the spleen (Figure 3—figure supplement 4A) of infected mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7 supplement 1D and Figure 3 supplement 4A.

claim: CD44hiGzB+PRF+ CD4+ T cells compose the subset of activated cells among which the higher frequencies of cells expressing Lag-3, Tim-3, CD39 and PD-1 are found, both in the spleen and in the heart.
source: Results in Figure 7—figure supplement 3, show that CD44hiGzB+PRF+ CD4+ T cells compose the subset of activated cells among which the higher frequencies of cells expressing these markers are found, both in the spleen and in the heart, at day 14 pi.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7 supplement 3 showing marker expression frequencies.

claim: The intensity of expression of PD-1 is significantly higher among CD44hiGzB+PRF+ (CD4CTLs) compared to CD44hiGzB-PRF- CD4+ T cells infiltrating the cardiac tissue.
source: However, the intensity of expression of the PD-1 marker was significantly higher among CD44hiGzB+PRF+ (CD4CTLs) compared to CD44hiGzB-PRF- CD4+ T cells infiltrating the cardiac tissue.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data showing mean fluorescence intensity of PD-1 expression.

claim: Mean fluorescence intensity values of Tim-3, CD39 and PD-1 expression are increased on CD4CTLs in the heart compared to CD4CTLs in the spleen.
source: Of note, while mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) values of Tim-3, CD39 and PD-1 expression were increased on CD4CTLs in the heart compared to CD4CTLs in the spleen, Lag-3 expression levels were decreased on CD4CTLs infiltrating the myocardium.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7 supplement 4 comparing marker expression in heart and spleen.

claim: Lag-3 expression levels are decreased on CD4CTLs infiltrating the myocardium compared to CD4CTLs in the spleen.
source: while mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) values of Tim-3, CD39 and PD-1 expression were increased on CD4CTLs in the heart compared to CD4CTLs in the spleen, Lag-3 expression levels were decreased on CD4CTLs infiltrating the myocardium.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data comparing Lag-3 expression in heart and spleen.

claim: Only the expression of PD-1, but not of Lag-3, Tim-3 or CD39, is upregulated on CD8CTLs in the heart compared to the spleen.
source: Furthermore, only the expression of PD-1, but not of Lag-3, Tim-3 or CD39, is upregulated on CD8CTLs in the heart compared to the spleen (Figure 7—figure supplement 4)
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7 supplement 4 comparing CD8CTL marker expression.

claim: The T. cruzi-infected cardiac tissue is a less exhaustion-inducing environment compared to certain tumors.
source: an indication that the T. cruzi-infected cardiac tissue is a less so-called exhaustion-inducing environment compared to certain tumors.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the differential expression patterns of exhaustion markers compared to what is known in tumor environments.

claim: After incubation with trypomastigote-derived antigens, both the expression level of PRF (MFI) and the percentage of PRF+CD4+ T cells increase among CD4+ T cells from chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy patients, but not from healthy donor controls.
source: As shown in Figure 7G and H, after incubation with trypo, both the expression level of PRF (MFI) and the percentage of PRF+CD4+ T cells increased among CD4+ T cells from CC patients, but not from HD controls.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7G and H from human PBMC experiments.

claim: CD4+ T cells expressing PRF are found at higher frequency in chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy patients than in healthy donors.
source: Of note, CD4+ T cells expressing PRF were found at higher frequency in CC patients than in HD (Figure 7I).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7I comparing patient and control groups.

claim: There is a clear inverse correlation between the frequency of CD4+PRF+ T cells and left ventricular ejection fraction in chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy patients.
source: As shown in Figure 7J and a clear inverse correlation between the frequency of CD4+PRF+ T cells and LVEF, as well as a direct correlation between the frequency of these cells and the left atrium diameter was found.
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 7J.

claim: There is a direct correlation between the frequency of CD4+PRF+ T cells and left atrium diameter in chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy patients.
source: a clear inverse correlation between the frequency of CD4+PRF+ T cells and LVEF, as well as a direct correlation between the frequency of these cells and the left atrium diameter was found.
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 7J.

claim: CD4CTLs might play a pathogenic role in the chronic phase of Chagas disease.
source: These correlations suggest that CD4CTLs might play a pathogenic role in the chronic phase of Chagas disease, although the alternative possibility remains that the higher levels of CD4CTLs reflect elevated parasite burden and/or inflammation in the heart, without a direct involvement of this cell subset in the pathology.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on correlation data but acknowledging alternative explanations.

claim: The heart is an important target-organ for CD4+ T cells with cytolytic potential generated in response to infection with T. cruzi.
source: Together, data obtained here in CC patients and in the mouse experimental model point to the heart as an important target-organ for CD4+ T cells with cytolytic potential generated in response to infection with T. cruzi.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from data showing enrichment of CD4CTLs in infected hearts and their presence in Chagas patients.

claim: Chagas disease is one of the most important parasitic diseases in the Western Hemisphere.
source: T. cruzi is an intracellular protozoan parasite and the etiologic agent of Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis), one of the most important parasitic diseases in the Western Hemisphere.
evidence: The claim represents established scientific knowledge about Chagas disease.

claim: Chagas disease is an important cause of heart failure, stroke, arrhythmia, and sudden death.
source: Chagas disease is an important cause of heart failure, stroke, arrhythmia, and sudden death, being the leading cause of cardiomyopathy among younger individuals in Latin America (Bern, 2015; Nunes et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Bern, 2015; Nunes et al., 2018).

claim: Chagas disease is the leading cause of cardiomyopathy among younger individuals in Latin America.
source: being the leading cause of cardiomyopathy among younger individuals in Latin America (Bern, 2015; Nunes et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Bern, 2015; Nunes et al., 2018).

claim: Myd88-/- mice are highly susceptible to infection with T. cruzi.
source: the fact that Myd88-/- mice have lower levels of Th1 cells and are highly susceptible to infection with T. cruzi (Campos et al., 2004; Oliveira et al., 2010)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Campos et al., 2004; Oliveira et al., 2010).

claim: Il18ra-/- mouse lineage is very susceptible to infection with T. cruzi.
source: The Il18ra-/- mouse lineage was previously shown to be very susceptible to infection with T. cruzi (Oliveira et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Oliveira et al., 2017).

claim: IFN-γ expression by CD4+ T cells is necessary for decreasing parasitemia.
source: Although IFN-γ expression by CD4+ T cells is necessary for decreasing parasitemia (Oliveira et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Oliveira et al., 2017).

claim: Tr1 cells are a subset of IL-10-producing CD4+FoxP3- T cells that express GzB and PRF and exert a potent suppressive function both in humans and mice.
source: Tr1 cells are a subset of IL-10-producing CD4+FoxP3- T cells that express GzB and PRF and exert a potent suppressive function both in humans and mice (Roncarolo et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Roncarolo et al., 2018).

claim: Eomes drives the development of Tr1 cells.
source: Since a high percentage of CD4+GzB+ T cells in our system express Eomes, which drives the development of Tr1 cells (Zhang et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work (Zhang et al., 2017).
